grade.first_issue: None; the proof is complete and correct.
grade.summary: The lexicographic potential (N,V) proves termination: coprime selections decrease N, while selections with nontrivial gcd either decrease N or, when both outputs remain greater than 1, strictly decrease V. The process always retains at least one entry greater than 1, so termination leaves exactly one. Primewise, each move applies a subtraction step to the two valuations and preserves their gcd; hence the gcd of all valuations for each prime is invariant and reconstructs the unique terminal integer. This establishes independence of all choices.
strengths: The proposed potential is well-founded and its change is calculated correctly in every case.
The argument correctly proves that a terminal board has exactly one entry greater than 1.
The primewise Euclidean-algorithm invariant is valid and yields an explicit formula for the terminal value.
All essential quantifiers and both requested conclusions are addressed.
